# lib.rs - source

Source: https://docs.rs/libyml/0.0.6/src/libyml/lib.rs.html

# libyml/lib.rs

[1](https://docs.rs#1)// SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT OR Apache-2.0
[2](https://docs.rs#2)
[3](https://docs.rs#3)//! # ⚠️ `libyml` is deprecated — migrate to a maintained alternative
[4](https://docs.rs#4)//!
[5](https://docs.rs#5)//! This crate is **unmaintained**. The `0.0.6` release is a thin
[6](https://docs.rs#6)//! compatibility shim so existing call sites keep working while you
[7](https://docs.rs#7)//! plan a migration. See [`MIGRATION.md`](https://github.com/sebastienrousseau/libyml/blob/master/MIGRATION.md)
[8](https://docs.rs#8)//! for the full guide.
[9](https://docs.rs#9)//!
[10](https://docs.rs#10)//! ## Maintained alternatives
[11](https://docs.rs#11)//!
[12](https://docs.rs#12)//! - **[`unsafe-libyaml`](https://crates.io/crates/unsafe-libyaml)**
[13](https://docs.rs#13)//!   — the upstream Rust translation of C `libyaml` that `libyml`
[14](https://docs.rs#14)//!   was originally forked from. Same `yaml_*` function surface,
[15](https://docs.rs#15)//!   actively maintained. **Drop-in replacement** for users on the
[16](https://docs.rs#16)//!   raw FFI-shaped API.
[17](https://docs.rs#17)//! - **[`yaml-rust2`](https://crates.io/crates/yaml-rust2)** —
[18](https://docs.rs#18)//!   pure-Rust low-level parser, no FFI. Returns a `Yaml` enum AST
[19](https://docs.rs#19)//!   instead of the event-stream model. Fits users who want to move
[20](https://docs.rs#20)//!   off the C-libyaml shape entirely while keeping a low-level
[21](https://docs.rs#21)//!   parser primitive.
[22](https://docs.rs#22)//! - **[`noyalib`](https://crates.io/crates/noyalib)** — modern,
[23](https://docs.rs#23)//!   pure-Rust, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` YAML library with a
[24](https://docs.rs#24)//!   high-level typed API (`from_str::<T>` / `Value`). Fits users
[25](https://docs.rs#25)//!   who can move from event-stream parsing to typed deserialisation.
[26](https://docs.rs#26)//!
[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! `MIGRATION.md` carries the per-crate mapping tables.
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//!
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! ## Why the shim is backed by `unsafe-libyaml`
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//!
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! `libyml` was originally a fork of `unsafe-libyaml` with cosmetic
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! renames (snake_case → PascalCase for type names). The 0.0.6 shim
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//! reverts those renames internally and re-exports the upstream's
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! functions and types, restoring the historical PascalCase aliases
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//! so existing call sites compile unchanged.
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//!
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! This is an implementation detail, not a recommendation that you
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! must use `unsafe-libyaml`. Two things follow:
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//!
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//! - **No duplicated `unsafe` translation in the dependency graph.**
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//!   Downstream users link the upstream's audited copy of the
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//!   C-libyaml translation rather than this fork's stale copy.
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//! - **Bug fixes flow through.** Anything fixed in
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//!   `unsafe-libyaml` lands in users of this shim on a plain
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//!   `cargo update`, without a new `libyml` release.
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! If you want to evaluate `yaml-rust2` or `noyalib` directly,
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//! `MIGRATION.md` covers both.
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//!
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! ## Stop-gap: keep using `libyml = "0.0.6"`
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//!
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! Existing call sites compile unchanged against this shim. Every
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! item below is marked `#[deprecated]`, so the compiler will point
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//! at the spots that need updating during your migration.
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//!
[56](https://docs.rs#56)//! ## What still resolves under `libyml::*` (0.0.6)
[57](https://docs.rs#57)//!
[58](https://docs.rs#58)//! Most of the previous public surface is **retained** via thin
[59](https://docs.rs#59)//! re-export modules pointing at `unsafe-libyaml`:
[60](https://docs.rs#60)//!
[61](https://docs.rs#61)//! - [`libyml::api`](crate::api) — parser/emitter init + event
[62](https://docs.rs#62)//!   initialisers.
[63](https://docs.rs#63)//! - [`libyml::decode`](crate::decode) — `yaml_parser_initialize`
[64](https://docs.rs#64)//!   / `_delete`.
[65](https://docs.rs#65)//! - [`libyml::document`](crate::document) — `yaml_document_*`
[66](https://docs.rs#66)//!   helpers.
[67](https://docs.rs#67)//! - [`libyml::dumper`](crate::dumper) — `yaml_emitter_open`
[68](https://docs.rs#68)//!   / `_close` / `_dump`.
[69](https://docs.rs#69)//! - [`libyml::loader`](crate::loader) — `yaml_parser_load`.
[70](https://docs.rs#70)//! - [`libyml::yaml`](crate::yaml) — every PascalCase type alias
[71](https://docs.rs#71)//!   and PascalCase enum-variant constant.
[72](https://docs.rs#72)//! - [`libyml::success`](crate::success) — `is_success(bool)` /
[73](https://docs.rs#73)//!   `is_failure(bool)` helpers (the `Success` struct itself is
[74](https://docs.rs#74)//!   no longer nameable — read `.ok` instead).
[75](https://docs.rs#75)//!
[76](https://docs.rs#76)//! The historical [`libyml::memory`](crate::memory) and
[77](https://docs.rs#77)//! [`libyml::string`](crate::string) paths still resolve, but as
[78](https://docs.rs#78)//! **empty stub modules** — every former item under them is gone
[79](https://docs.rs#79)//! because they belonged to the hand-translated C copy this shim
[80](https://docs.rs#80)//! deletes (`libyml::string::yaml_string_extend` is the unsound
[81](https://docs.rs#81)//! helper RUSTSEC-2025-0067 flags).
[82](https://docs.rs#82)//!
[83](https://docs.rs#83)//! ## Removed in 0.0.6 (vs. 0.0.5)
[84](https://docs.rs#84)//!
[85](https://docs.rs#85)//! The implementation-detail modules — `libyml::internal`,
[86](https://docs.rs#86)//! `libyml::macros`, `libyml::externs`, `libyml::utils`,
[87](https://docs.rs#87)//! `libyml::libc`, the contents of `libyml::memory` and
[88](https://docs.rs#88)//! `libyml::string`, and the `yaml-test-suite` runner binaries
[89](https://docs.rs#89)//! under `src/bin/` — are **gone** in this release. See
[90](https://docs.rs#90)//! `MIGRATION.md` for the equivalence table per alternative.
[91](https://docs.rs#91)
[92](https://docs.rs#92)#![deprecated(
[93](https://docs.rs#93)    since = "0.0.6",
[94](https://docs.rs#94)    note = "libyml is unmaintained. Migrate to a maintained alternative (unsafe-libyaml, yaml-rust2, or noyalib). See MIGRATION.md."
[95](https://docs.rs#95))]
[96](https://docs.rs#96)#![doc(html_root_url = "https://docs.rs/libyml/0.0.6")]
[97](https://docs.rs#97)#![no_std]
[98](https://docs.rs#98)// The PascalCase `pub const Yaml*` aliases below intentionally
[99](https://docs.rs#99)// shadow the upstream's SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE variants so existing
[100](https://docs.rs#100)// `libyml`-flavoured call sites compile unchanged. The
[101](https://docs.rs#101)// `non_upper_case_globals` lint flags this naming convention as
[102](https://docs.rs#102)// non-idiomatic; the alias is the entire point.
[103](https://docs.rs#103)#![allow(non_upper_case_globals)]
[104](https://docs.rs#104)

[106](https://docs.rs#106)

[130](https://docs.rs#130)// ── Type aliases — restore the PascalCase names libyml ≤ 0.0.5 used ────
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//
[132](https://docs.rs#132)// `unsafe-libyaml` uses C-style snake_case (`yaml_event_t`,
[133](https://docs.rs#133)// `yaml_parser_t`, …); `libyml` historically renamed those to
[134](https://docs.rs#134)// PascalCase (`YamlEventT`, `YamlParserT`, …). The aliases below
[135](https://docs.rs#135)// preserve the historical name surface so `use libyml::YamlParserT`
[136](https://docs.rs#136)// keeps resolving.

[193](https://docs.rs#193)
[194](https://docs.rs#194)// ── Enum-variant re-exports ───────────────────────────────────────────
[195](https://docs.rs#195)//
[196](https://docs.rs#196)// `libyml` ≤ 0.0.5 named its enum variants in PascalCase
[197](https://docs.rs#197)// (`YamlUtf8Encoding`, `YamlPlainScalarStyle`, …) and re-exported
[198](https://docs.rs#198)// them at the crate root via `pub use crate::yaml::*::*`.
[199](https://docs.rs#199)// `unsafe-libyaml` keeps the C convention — SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE
[200](https://docs.rs#200)// (`YAML_UTF8_ENCODING`, `YAML_PLAIN_SCALAR_STYLE`, …).
[201](https://docs.rs#201)//
[202](https://docs.rs#202)// To preserve the historical bare-name surface, this section
[203](https://docs.rs#203)// declares `pub const`s that alias each PascalCase name to the
[204](https://docs.rs#204)// equivalent upstream variant. The aliases work in **value
[205](https://docs.rs#205)// position** (`yaml_emitter_set_encoding(emit, YamlUtf8Encoding)`)
[206](https://docs.rs#206)// — which is the overwhelming majority of usages — but **not as
[207](https://docs.rs#207)// refutable patterns** in `match` arms, where the upstream
[208](https://docs.rs#208)// SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE name is required. The MIGRATION.md guide
[209](https://docs.rs#209)// documents this delta.
[210](https://docs.rs#210)//
[211](https://docs.rs#211)// The deep parser/emitter state-machine enums (`YamlParserStateT`,
[212](https://docs.rs#212)// `YamlEmitterStateT`) had ~30 variants each and were never part
[213](https://docs.rs#213)// of typical user code; their variants are reachable through the
[214](https://docs.rs#214)// upstream's snake_case path (`unsafe_libyaml::YAML_PARSE_*`).
[215](https://docs.rs#215)
[216](https://docs.rs#216)/// Re-export of upstream variants under their original SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE
[217](https://docs.rs#217)/// names. Available for users who want to opt into the upstream surface
[218](https://docs.rs#218)/// without renaming.
[219](https://docs.rs#219)#[doc(hidden)]
[220](https://docs.rs#220)pub use unsafe_libyaml::{
[221](https://docs.rs#221)    YAML_ALIAS_EVENT, YAML_ALIAS_TOKEN, YAML_ANCHOR_TOKEN,
[222](https://docs.rs#222)    YAML_ANY_ENCODING, YAML_ANY_MAPPING_STYLE, YAML_ANY_SCALAR_STYLE,
[223](https://docs.rs#223)    YAML_ANY_SEQUENCE_STYLE, YAML_BLOCK_END_TOKEN,
[224](https://docs.rs#224)    YAML_BLOCK_ENTRY_TOKEN, YAML_BLOCK_MAPPING_START_TOKEN,
[225](https://docs.rs#225)    YAML_BLOCK_MAPPING_STYLE, YAML_BLOCK_SEQUENCE_START_TOKEN,
[226](https://docs.rs#226)    YAML_BLOCK_SEQUENCE_STYLE, YAML_COMPOSER_ERROR,
[227](https://docs.rs#227)    YAML_DOCUMENT_END_EVENT, YAML_DOCUMENT_END_TOKEN,
[228](https://docs.rs#228)    YAML_DOCUMENT_START_EVENT, YAML_DOCUMENT_START_TOKEN,
[229](https://docs.rs#229)    YAML_DOUBLE_QUOTED_SCALAR_STYLE, YAML_EMITTER_ERROR,
[230](https://docs.rs#230)    YAML_FLOW_ENTRY_TOKEN, YAML_FLOW_MAPPING_END_TOKEN,
[231](https://docs.rs#231)    YAML_FLOW_MAPPING_START_TOKEN, YAML_FLOW_MAPPING_STYLE,
[232](https://docs.rs#232)    YAML_FLOW_SEQUENCE_END_TOKEN, YAML_FLOW_SEQUENCE_START_TOKEN,
[233](https://docs.rs#233)    YAML_FLOW_SEQUENCE_STYLE, YAML_FOLDED_SCALAR_STYLE, YAML_KEY_TOKEN,
[234](https://docs.rs#234)    YAML_LITERAL_SCALAR_STYLE, YAML_MAPPING_END_EVENT,
[235](https://docs.rs#235)    YAML_MAPPING_NODE, YAML_MAPPING_START_EVENT, YAML_MEMORY_ERROR,
[236](https://docs.rs#236)    YAML_NO_ERROR, YAML_NO_EVENT, YAML_NO_NODE, YAML_NO_TOKEN,
[237](https://docs.rs#237)    YAML_PARSER_ERROR, YAML_PLAIN_SCALAR_STYLE, YAML_READER_ERROR,

[371](https://docs.rs#371)// ── `libyml::success` — keep path-form imports working ────────────────
[372](https://docs.rs#372)
[373](https://docs.rs#373)/// Success/failure helpers retained for source compatibility with
[374](https://docs.rs#374)/// `libyml ≤ 0.0.5`.
[375](https://docs.rs#375)///
[376](https://docs.rs#376)/// **Migration note.** The upstream `unsafe-libyaml` crate keeps its
[377](https://docs.rs#377)/// `Success` / `Failure` structs in a private module — the values
[378](https://docs.rs#378)/// flow out of `yaml_*` calls but cannot be named at a path. The
[379](https://docs.rs#379)/// previous `libyml::success::Success` type therefore has **no
[380](https://docs.rs#380)/// nameable equivalent in the shim**; the public helpers below
[381](https://docs.rs#381)/// accept `bool` so they can still chain with the upstream return
[382](https://docs.rs#382)/// values via `.ok`.
[383](https://docs.rs#383)///
[384](https://docs.rs#384)/// Old:
[385](https://docs.rs#385)///
[386](https://docs.rs#386)/// ```ignore
[387](https://docs.rs#387)/// use libyml::success::is_success;
[388](https://docs.rs#388)/// if is_success(yaml_parser_initialize(p)) { /* … */ }
[389](https://docs.rs#389)/// ```
[390](https://docs.rs#390)///
[391](https://docs.rs#391)/// New:
[392](https://docs.rs#392)///
[393](https://docs.rs#393)/// ```ignore
[394](https://docs.rs#394)/// use libyml::success::is_success;
[395](https://docs.rs#395)/// if is_success(yaml_parser_initialize(p).ok) { /* … */ }
[396](https://docs.rs#396)/// ```
[397](https://docs.rs#397)pub mod success {
[398](https://docs.rs#398)    /// Returns `true` when the operation was successful.
[399](https://docs.rs#399)    ///
[400](https://docs.rs#400)    /// Historical `libyml ≤ 0.0.5` helper. Now takes the `ok`
[401](https://docs.rs#401)    /// flag of the upstream `Success` struct directly.
[402](https://docs.rs#402)    pub fn is_success(ok: bool) -> bool {
[403](https://docs.rs#403)        ok
[404](https://docs.rs#404)    }
[405](https://docs.rs#405)
[406](https://docs.rs#406)    /// Returns `true` when the operation failed.
[407](https://docs.rs#407)    ///
[408](https://docs.rs#408)    /// Historical `libyml ≤ 0.0.5` helper. Now takes the `ok`
[409](https://docs.rs#409)    /// flag of the upstream `Success` struct directly.
[410](https://docs.rs#410)    pub fn is_failure(ok: bool) -> bool {
[411](https://docs.rs#411)        !ok
[412](https://docs.rs#412)    }
[413](https://docs.rs#413)}
[414](https://docs.rs#414)
[415](https://docs.rs#415)// ── Path-form re-export modules ───────────────────────────────────────
[416](https://docs.rs#416)//
[417](https://docs.rs#417)// `libyml ≤ 0.0.5` exposed its surface under several sub-modules so
[418](https://docs.rs#418)// callers could do `use libyml::api::yaml_parser_set_input_string` or
[419](https://docs.rs#419)// `use libyml::yaml::YamlEventT`. The modules below restore those
[420](https://docs.rs#420)// paths verbatim by re-exporting the equivalent items from the crate
[421](https://docs.rs#421)// root (which itself re-exports from `unsafe-libyaml`). Every item is
[422](https://docs.rs#422)// inherits the `#[deprecated]` annotation through the crate root, so
[423](https://docs.rs#423)// the compiler still points at every usage during migration.
[424](https://docs.rs#424)
[425](https://docs.rs#425)/// API-surface helpers. Re-exported from the crate root for source
[426](https://docs.rs#426)/// compatibility with `libyml ≤ 0.0.5`'s
[427](https://docs.rs#427)/// [`libyml::api`](https://docs.rs/libyml/0.0.5/libyml/api/index.html)
[428](https://docs.rs#428)/// module.
[429](https://docs.rs#429)pub mod api {
[430](https://docs.rs#430)    pub use crate::{
[431](https://docs.rs#431)        yaml_alias_event_initialize, yaml_emitter_delete,
[432](https://docs.rs#432)        yaml_emitter_initialize, yaml_emitter_set_break,
[433](https://docs.rs#433)        yaml_emitter_set_canonical, yaml_emitter_set_encoding,
[434](https://docs.rs#434)        yaml_emitter_set_indent, yaml_emitter_set_output,
[435](https://docs.rs#435)        yaml_emitter_set_output_string, yaml_emitter_set_unicode,
[436](https://docs.rs#436)        yaml_emitter_set_width, yaml_mapping_end_event_initialize,
[437](https://docs.rs#437)        yaml_mapping_start_event_initialize, yaml_parser_set_encoding,
[438](https://docs.rs#438)        yaml_parser_set_input, yaml_parser_set_input_string,
[439](https://docs.rs#439)        yaml_scalar_event_initialize,
[440](https://docs.rs#440)        yaml_sequence_end_event_initialize,
[441](https://docs.rs#441)        yaml_sequence_start_event_initialize,
[442](https://docs.rs#442)        yaml_stream_end_event_initialize,
[443](https://docs.rs#443)        yaml_stream_start_event_initialize, yaml_token_delete,
[444](https://docs.rs#444)    };
[445](https://docs.rs#445)}

[530](https://docs.rs#530)    /// Alias for [`u8`]. `libyml ≤ 0.0.5` exposed YAML scalar bytes
[531](https://docs.rs#531)    /// as `yaml_char_t` (the `libyaml` C convention); preserved here
[532](https://docs.rs#532)    /// for source compatibility.

[534](https://docs.rs#534)    pub type yaml_char_t = u8;
[535](https://docs.rs#535)}
[536](https://docs.rs#536)
[537](https://docs.rs#537)/// **Removed in 0.0.6.** Previous releases exposed a hand-translated
[538](https://docs.rs#538)/// C-libyaml allocator surface (`yaml_malloc` / `yaml_free` /
[539](https://docs.rs#539)/// `yaml_realloc` / `yaml_strdup`). Those helpers were
[540](https://docs.rs#540)/// implementation details of the hand-translated parser, which the
[541](https://docs.rs#541)/// 0.0.6 shim deletes; the upstream `unsafe-libyaml` uses Rust's
[542](https://docs.rs#542)/// `alloc` directly. Allocate with Rust's standard primitives
[543](https://docs.rs#543)/// instead. This empty module is retained so that
[544](https://docs.rs#544)/// `use libyml::memory;` keeps resolving — every former item under
[545](https://docs.rs#545)/// it is gone.
[546](https://docs.rs#546)pub mod memory {}
[547](https://docs.rs#547)
[548](https://docs.rs#548)/// **Removed in 0.0.6 — see [`RUSTSEC-2025-0067`].** Previous
[549](https://docs.rs#549)/// releases exposed `yaml_string_extend` / `yaml_string_join`
[550](https://docs.rs#550)/// helpers under this path. The 0.0.6 shim deletes the entire
[551](https://docs.rs#551)/// hand-translated C copy that those helpers belonged to. Build
[552](https://docs.rs#552)/// strings with Rust's `Vec` / `String` instead. This empty module
[553](https://docs.rs#553)/// is retained so `use libyml::string;` keeps resolving — every
[554](https://docs.rs#554)/// former item under it is gone.
[555](https://docs.rs#555)///
[556](https://docs.rs#556)/// [`RUSTSEC-2025-0067`]: https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2025-0067.html
[557](https://docs.rs#557)pub mod string {}

# libyml::memory - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/libyml/0.0.6/libyml/memory/index.html

libyml is unmaintained. Migrate to a maintained alternative (unsafe-libyaml, yaml-rust2, or noyalib). See MIGRATION.md.

## Expand description

**Removed in 0.0.6.** Previous releases exposed a hand-translated
C-libyaml allocator surface (`yaml_malloc` / `yaml_free` /
`yaml_realloc` / `yaml_strdup`). Those helpers were
implementation details of the hand-translated parser, which the
0.0.6 shim deletes; the upstream `unsafe-libyaml` uses Rust’s
`alloc` directly. Allocate with Rust’s standard primitives
instead. This empty module is retained so that
`use libyml::memory;` keeps resolving — every former item under
it is gone.

---

# yaml_document_end_event_initialize in libyml - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/libyml/0.0.6/libyml/fn.yaml_document_end_event_initialize.html

```
pub unsafe fn yaml_document_end_event_initialize(
    event:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_event_t](https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml/0.2.11/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/unsafe_libyaml/yaml/struct.yaml_event_t.html),
    implicit: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.bool.html),
) -> Success## Expand description

Create the DOCUMENT-END event.

The `implicit` argument is considered as a stylistic parameter and may be
ignored by the emitter.

```
39fn emit_simple_document() {
40    unsafe {
41        let mut emitter = MaybeUninit::<YamlEmitterT>::uninit();
42        assert!(is_success(
43            yaml_emitter_initialize(emitter.as_mut_ptr()).ok
44        ));
45        let mut emitter = emitter.assume_init();
46
47        let mut buf = [0u8; 128];
48        let mut size_written: u64 = 0;
49        yaml_emitter_set_output_string(
50            &mut emitter,
51            buf.as_mut_ptr(),
52            buf.len() as u64,
53            &mut size_written,
54        );
55
56        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
57            yaml_stream_start_event_initialize(ev, YamlUtf8Encoding).ok
58        });
59        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
60            unsafe_libyaml::yaml_document_start_event_initialize(
61                ev,
62                ptr::null_mut(),
63                ptr::null_mut(),
64                ptr::null_mut(),
65                true,
66            )
67            .ok
68        });
69        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
70            yaml_mapping_start_event_initialize(
71                ev,
72                ptr::null_mut(),
73                ptr::null_mut(),
74                true,
75                YamlBlockMappingStyle,
76            )
77            .ok
78        });
79        let key = b"hello\0";
80        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
81            yaml_scalar_event_initialize(
82                ev,
83                ptr::null_mut(),
84                ptr::null_mut(),
85                key.as_ptr(),
86                (key.len() - 1) as i32,
87                true,
88                true,
89                YamlPlainScalarStyle,
90            )
91            .ok
92        });
93        let val = b"world\0";
94        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
95            yaml_scalar_event_initialize(
96                ev,
97                ptr::null_mut(),
98                ptr::null_mut(),
99                val.as_ptr(),
100                (val.len() - 1) as i32,
101                true,
102                true,
103                YamlPlainScalarStyle,
104            )
105            .ok
106        });
107        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
108            yaml_mapping_end_event_initialize(ev).ok
109        });
110        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
111            unsafe_libyaml::yaml_document_end_event_initialize(ev, true)
112                .ok
113        });
114        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
115            yaml_stream_end_event_initialize(ev).ok
116        });
117
118        let out = core::str::from_utf8(&buf[..size_written as usize])
119            .unwrap();
120        println!("✅ emitter produced:\n{out}");
121
122        yaml_emitter_delete(&mut emitter);
123    }
124}
```

---

# yaml_document_get_root_node in libyml - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/libyml/0.0.6/libyml/fn.yaml_document_get_root_node.html

```
pub unsafe fn yaml_document_get_root_node(
    document:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_document_t](https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml/0.2.11/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/unsafe_libyaml/yaml/struct.yaml_document_t.html),
) -> [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_node_t](https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml/0.2.11/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/unsafe_libyaml/yaml/struct.yaml_node_t.html)## Expand description

Get the root of a YAML document node.

The root object is the first object added to the document.

The pointer returned by this function is valid until any of the functions modifying the documents are called.

An empty document produced by the parser signifies the end of a YAML stream.

Returns the node object or NULL if the document is empty.

Emit a YAML document.

The document object may be generated using the yaml_parser_load() function or the yaml_document_initialize() function. The emitter takes the responsibility for the document object and destroys its content after it is emitted. The document object is destroyed even if the function fails.

[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_emitter_t](https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml/0.2.11/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/unsafe_libyaml/yaml/struct.yaml_emitter_t.html),

Set a string output.

The emitter will write the output characters to the `output` buffer of the
size `size`. The emitter will set `size_written` to the number of written
bytes. If the buffer is smaller than required, the emitter produces the
YAML_WRITE_ERROR error.

42        assert!(is_success(
43            yaml_emitter_initialize(emitter.as_mut_ptr()).ok
44        ));
45        let mut emitter = emitter.assume_init();
46
47        let mut buf = [0u8; 128];
48        let mut size_written: u64 = 0;
49        yaml_emitter_set_output_string(
50            &mut emitter,
51            buf.as_mut_ptr(),
52            buf.len() as u64,
53            &mut size_written,
54        );
55
56        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
57            yaml_stream_start_event_initialize(ev, YamlUtf8Encoding).ok
58        });
59        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
60            unsafe_libyaml::yaml_document_start_event_initialize(
61                ev,
62                ptr::null_mut(),
63                ptr::null_mut(),
64                ptr::null_mut(),
65                true,
66            )
67            .ok
68        });
69        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
70            yaml_mapping_start_event_initialize(
71                ev,
72                ptr::null_mut(),
73                ptr::null_mut(),
74                true,
75                YamlBlockMappingStyle,
76            )
77            .ok
78        });
79        let key = b"hello\0";
80        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
81            yaml_scalar_event_initialize(
82                ev,
83                ptr::null_mut(),
84                ptr::null_mut(),
85                key.as_ptr(),
86                (key.len() - 1) as i32,
87                true,
88                true,
89                YamlPlainScalarStyle,
90            )
91            .ok
92        });
93        let val = b"world\0";
94        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
95            yaml_scalar_event_initialize(
96                ev,
97                ptr::null_mut(),
98                ptr::null_mut(),
99                val.as_ptr(),
100                (val.len() - 1) as i32,
101                true,
102                true,
103                YamlPlainScalarStyle,
104            )
105            .ok
106        });
107        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
108            yaml_mapping_end_event_initialize(ev).ok
109        });
110        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
111            unsafe_libyaml::yaml_document_end_event_initialize(ev, true)
112                .ok
113        });
114        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
115            yaml_stream_end_event_initialize(ev).ok
116        });
117
118        let out = core::str::from_utf8(&buf[..size_written as usize])
119            .unwrap();
120        println!("✅ emitter produced:\n{out}");
121
122        yaml_emitter_delete(&mut emitter);
123    }
124}
```

---

# yaml_parser_delete in libyml - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/libyml/0.0.6/libyml/fn.yaml_parser_delete.html

`pub unsafe fn yaml_parser_delete(parser: `[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_parser_t](https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml/0.2.11/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/unsafe_libyaml/yaml/struct.yaml_parser_t.html))## Expand description

Destroy a parser.

```
31fn main() {
32    let yaml = b"title: MyApp\nport: 8080\n";
33
34    unsafe {
35        let mut parser = MaybeUninit::<YamlParserT>::uninit();
36        assert!(is_success(
37            yaml_parser_initialize(parser.as_mut_ptr()).ok
38        ));
39        let mut parser = parser.assume_init();
40
41        yaml_parser_set_input_string(
42            &mut parser,
43            yaml.as_ptr(),
44            yaml.len() as u64,
45        );
46
47        let mut event_count = 0_u32;
48        loop {
49            let mut event = MaybeUninit::<YamlEventT>::uninit();
50            if !is_success(
51                yaml_parser_parse(&mut parser, event.as_mut_ptr()).ok,
52            ) {
53                eprintln!("parse failed");
54                break;
55            }
56            let event = event.assume_init();
57            event_count += 1;
58            if event.type_ == YamlStreamEndEvent
59                || event.type_ == YamlNoEvent
60            {
61                break;
62            }
63        }
64        println!(
65            "parsed {event_count} events from {} bytes",
66            yaml.len()
67        );
68
69        yaml_parser_delete(&mut parser);
70    }
71}
```
## More examples

```
20pub(crate) fn main() {
21    println!("\n❯ Executing examples/apis/main.rs");
22
23    let mut parser = MaybeUninit::uninit();
24    let parser_ptr = parser.as_mut_ptr();
25
26    unsafe {
27        let _ = yaml_parser_initialize(parser_ptr);
28        println!("✅ Successfully initialized the YAML parser");
29
30        let input = b"key: value\n";
31        yaml_parser_set_input_string(
32            parser_ptr,
33            input.as_ptr(),
34            input.len().try_into().unwrap(),
35        );
36        println!(
37            "✅ Successfully set the input string for the YAML parser"
38        );
39
40        // ── Removed slab #1: `libyml::memory::*` (C-libyaml allocator)
41        //
42        // The previous example demoed `yaml_malloc` / `yaml_realloc`
43        // / `yaml_strdup` / `yaml_free`. The 0.0.6 shim deletes the
44        // entire `libyml::memory` surface because the upstream
45        // `unsafe-libyaml` uses Rust's `alloc` directly — the
46        // C-style allocator wrappers are no longer needed.
47        //
48        // Migration:
49        //
50        //     use std::alloc::{alloc, dealloc, Layout};
51        //     let layout = Layout::from_size_align(1024, 8).unwrap();
52        //     let ptr = unsafe { alloc(layout) };
53        //     /* ... use ptr ... */
54        //     unsafe { dealloc(ptr, layout) };
55
56        // ── Removed slab #2: `libyml::string::yaml_string_extend`
57        //
58        // The previous example demoed `yaml_string_extend` and
59        // `yaml_string_join` — the helpers
60        // [RUSTSEC-2025-0067](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2025-0067.html)
61        // flagged as unsound. The 0.0.6 shim deletes the entire
62        // `libyml::string` surface; build strings with Rust's
63        // standard primitives:
64        //
65        //     let mut buf: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
66        //     buf.extend_from_slice(b"Hello, ");
67        //     buf.extend_from_slice(b"world!");
68
69        yaml_parser_delete(parser_ptr);
70        println!("✅ Successfully deleted the YAML parser");
71    }
72}
```

# yaml_parser_load in libyml - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/libyml/0.0.6/libyml/fn.yaml_parser_load.html

```
pub unsafe fn yaml_parser_load(
    parser:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_parser_t](https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml/0.2.11/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/unsafe_libyaml/yaml/struct.yaml_parser_t.html),
    document: [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_document_t](https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml/0.2.11/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/unsafe_libyaml/yaml/struct.yaml_document_t.html),
) -> Success## Expand description

Parse the input stream and produce the next YAML document.

Call this function subsequently to produce a sequence of documents constituting the input stream.

If the produced document has no root node, it means that the document end has been reached.

An application is responsible for freeing any data associated with the produced document object using the yaml_document_delete() function.

An application must not alternate the calls of yaml_parser_load() with the calls of yaml_parser_scan() or yaml_parser_parse(). Doing this will break the parser.

---

# yaml_parser_parse in libyml - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/libyml/0.0.6/libyml/fn.yaml_parser_parse.html

```
pub unsafe fn yaml_parser_parse(
    parser:
```
[*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_parser_t](https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml/0.2.11/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/unsafe_libyaml/yaml/struct.yaml_parser_t.html),
    event: [*mut ](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/primitive.pointer.html)[yaml_event_t](https://docs.rs/unsafe-libyaml/0.2.11/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/unsafe_libyaml/yaml/struct.yaml_event_t.html),
) -> Success## Expand description

Parse the input stream and produce the next parsing event.

Call the function subsequently to produce a sequence of events corresponding to the input stream. The initial event has the type YAML_STREAM_START_EVENT while the ending event has the type YAML_STREAM_END_EVENT.

An application is responsible for freeing any buffers associated with the produced event object using the yaml_event_delete() function.

An application must not alternate the calls of yaml_parser_parse() with the calls of yaml_parser_scan() or yaml_parser_load(). Doing this will break the parser.

```

38        ));
39        let mut parser = parser.assume_init();
40
41        yaml_parser_set_input_string(
42            &mut parser,
43            yaml.as_ptr(),
44            yaml.len() as u64,
45        );
46
47        let mut event_count = 0_u32;
48        loop {
49            let mut event = MaybeUninit::<YamlEventT>::uninit();
50            if !is_success(
51                yaml_parser_parse(&mut parser, event.as_mut_ptr()).ok,
52            ) {
53                eprintln!("parse failed");
54                break;
55            }
56            let event = event.assume_init();
57            event_count += 1;
58            if event.type_ == YamlStreamEndEvent
59                || event.type_ == YamlNoEvent
60            {
61                break;
62            }
63        }

67        );

41        let mut emitter = MaybeUninit::<YamlEmitterT>::uninit();
42        assert!(is_success(
43            yaml_emitter_initialize(emitter.as_mut_ptr()).ok
44        ));
45        let mut emitter = emitter.assume_init();
46
47        let mut buf = [0u8; 128];
48        let mut size_written: u64 = 0;
49        yaml_emitter_set_output_string(
50            &mut emitter,
51            buf.as_mut_ptr(),
52            buf.len() as u64,
53            &mut size_written,
54        );
55
56        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
57            yaml_stream_start_event_initialize(ev, YamlUtf8Encoding).ok
58        });
59        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
60            unsafe_libyaml::yaml_document_start_event_initialize(
61                ev,
62                ptr::null_mut(),
63                ptr::null_mut(),
64                ptr::null_mut(),
65                true,
66            )
67            .ok
68        });
69        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
70            yaml_mapping_start_event_initialize(
71                ev,
72                ptr::null_mut(),
73                ptr::null_mut(),
74                true,
75                YamlBlockMappingStyle,
76            )
77            .ok
78        });
79        let key = b"hello\0";
80        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
81            yaml_scalar_event_initialize(
82                ev,
83                ptr::null_mut(),
84                ptr::null_mut(),
85                key.as_ptr(),
86                (key.len() - 1) as i32,
87                true,
88                true,
89                YamlPlainScalarStyle,
90            )
91            .ok
92        });
93        let val = b"world\0";
94        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
95            yaml_scalar_event_initialize(
96                ev,
97                ptr::null_mut(),
98                ptr::null_mut(),
99                val.as_ptr(),
100                (val.len() - 1) as i32,
101                true,
102                true,
103                YamlPlainScalarStyle,
104            )
105            .ok
106        });
107        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
108            yaml_mapping_end_event_initialize(ev).ok
109        });
110        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
111            unsafe_libyaml::yaml_document_end_event_initialize(ev, true)
112                .ok
113        });
114        emit(&mut emitter, |ev| {
115            yaml_stream_end_event_initialize(ev).ok
116        });
117
118        let out = core::str::from_utf8(&buf[..size_written as usize])
119            .unwrap();
120        println!("✅ emitter produced:\n{out}");
121
122        yaml_emitter_delete(&mut emitter);
123    }
124}
```

---

union {
    /// The stream parameters (for YAML_STREAM_START_EVENT).
    stream_start: struct {
        /// The document encoding.
        encoding: yaml_encoding_t,
    },
    /// The document parameters (for YAML_DOCUMENT_START_EVENT).
    document_start: struct {
        /// The version directive.
        version_directive: *mut yaml_version_directive_t,
        /// The list of tag directives.
        tag_directives: struct {
            /// The beginning of the tag directives list.
            start: *mut yaml_tag_directive_t,
            /// The end of the tag directives list.
            end: *mut yaml_tag_directive_t,
        },
        /// Is the document indicator implicit?
        implicit: i32,
    },
    /// The document end parameters (for YAML_DOCUMENT_END_EVENT).
    document_end: struct {
        /// Is the document end indicator implicit?
        implicit: i32,
    },
    /// The alias parameters (for YAML_ALIAS_EVENT).
    alias: struct {
        /// The anchor.
        anchor: *mut u8,
    },
    /// The scalar parameters (for YAML_SCALAR_EVENT).
    scalar: struct {
        /// The anchor.
        anchor: *mut u8,
        /// The tag.
        tag: *mut u8,
        /// The scalar value.
        value: *mut u8,
        /// The length of the scalar value.
        length: u64,
        /// Is the tag optional for the plain style?
        plain_implicit: i32,
        /// Is the tag optional for any non-plain style?
        quoted_implicit: i32,
        /// The scalar style.
        style: yaml_scalar_style_t,
    },
    /// The sequence parameters (for YAML_SEQUENCE_START_EVENT).
    sequence_start: struct {
        /// The anchor.
        anchor: *mut u8,
        /// The tag.

        /// Is the tag optional?
        implicit: i32,
        /// The sequence style.

        /// The tag.
        tag: *mut u8,
        /// Is the tag optional?
        implicit: i32,
        /// The mapping style.
        style: yaml_mapping_style_t,
    },

```
union {
    /// The stream start (for YAML_STREAM_START_TOKEN).
    stream_start: struct {
        /// The stream encoding.
        encoding: yaml_encoding_t,
    },
    /// The alias (for YAML_ALIAS_TOKEN).
    alias: struct {
        /// The alias value.
        value: *mut u8,
    },
    /// The anchor (for YAML_ANCHOR_TOKEN).
    anchor: struct {
        /// The anchor value.
        value: *mut u8,
    },
    /// The tag (for YAML_TAG_TOKEN).
    tag: struct {
        /// The tag handle.
        handle: *mut u8,
        /// The tag suffix.
        suffix: *mut u8,
    },
    /// The scalar value (for YAML_SCALAR_TOKEN).
    scalar: struct {
        /// The scalar value.
        value: *mut u8,
        /// The length of the scalar value.
        length: u64,
        /// The scalar style.
        style: yaml_scalar_style_t,
    },
    /// The version directive (for YAML_VERSION_DIRECTIVE_TOKEN).
    version_directive: struct {
        /// The major version number.
        major: i32,
        /// The minor version number.
        minor: i32,
    },
    /// The tag directive (for YAML_TAG_DIRECTIVE_TOKEN).
    tag_directive: struct {
        /// The tag handle.
        handle: *mut u8,
        /// The tag prefix.
        prefix: *mut u8,
    },
}

# libyml - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/libyml/latest/libyml/

libyml is unmaintained. Migrate to a maintained alternative (unsafe-libyaml, yaml-rust2, or noyalib). See MIGRATION.md.

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#-libyml-is-deprecated--migrate-to-a-maintained-alternative)⚠️ `libyml` is deprecated — migrate to a maintained alternative

This crate is **unmaintained**. The `0.0.6` release is a thin
compatibility shim so existing call sites keep working while you
plan a migration. See [ MIGRATION.md](https://github.com/sebastienrousseau/libyml/blob/master/MIGRATION.md)
for the full guide.

[§](https://docs.rs#maintained-alternatives)Maintained alternatives

- `unsafe-libyaml`- `libyaml`that- `libyml`was originally forked from. Same- `yaml_*`function surface, actively maintained.- **Drop-in replacement**for users on the raw FFI-shaped API.
- `yaml-rust2`- `Yaml`enum AST instead of the event-stream model. Fits users who want to move off the C-libyaml shape entirely while keeping a low-level parser primitive.
- `noyalib`- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`YAML library with a high-level typed API (- `from_str::<T>`/- `Value`). Fits users who can move from event-stream parsing to typed deserialisation.

`MIGRATION.md` carries the per-crate mapping tables.

[§](https://docs.rs#why-the-shim-is-backed-by-unsafe-libyaml)Why the shim is backed by `unsafe-libyaml`

`libyml` was originally a fork of `unsafe-libyaml` with cosmetic
renames (snake_case → PascalCase for type names). The 0.0.6 shim
reverts those renames internally and re-exports the upstream’s
functions and types, restoring the historical PascalCase aliases
so existing call sites compile unchanged.

This is an implementation detail, not a recommendation that you
must use `unsafe-libyaml`. Two things follow:

- **No duplicated**Downstream users link the upstream’s audited copy of the C-libyaml translation rather than this fork’s stale copy.- `unsafe`translation in the dependency graph.
- **Bug fixes flow through.**Anything fixed in- `unsafe-libyaml`lands in users of this shim on a plain- `cargo update`, without a new- `libyml`release.

If you want to evaluate `yaml-rust2` or `noyalib` directly,
`MIGRATION.md` covers both.

[§](https://docs.rs#stop-gap-keep-using-libyml--006)Stop-gap: keep using `libyml = "0.0.6"`

Existing call sites compile unchanged against this shim. Every
item below is marked `#[deprecated]`, so the compiler will point
at the spots that need updating during your migration.

[§](https://docs.rs#what-still-resolves-under-libyml-006)What still resolves under `libyml::*` (0.0.6)

Most of the previous public surface is **retained** via thin
re-export modules pointing at `unsafe-libyaml`:

- `libyml::api`
- `libyml::decode`- `yaml_parser_initialize`/- `_delete`.
- `libyml::document`- `yaml_document_*`helpers.
- `libyml::dumper`- `yaml_emitter_open`/- `_close`/- `_dump`.
- `libyml::loader`- `yaml_parser_load`.
- `libyml::yaml`
- `libyml::success`- `is_success(bool)`/- `is_failure(bool)`helpers (the- `Success`struct itself is no longer nameable — read- `.ok`instead).

The historical [ libyml::memory](https://docs.rs/memory/index.html) and

[paths still resolve, but as](https://docs.rs/string/index.html)

`libyml::string`**empty stub modules**— every former item under them is gone because they belonged to the hand-translated C copy this shim deletes (

`libyml::string::yaml_string_extend` is the unsound
helper RUSTSEC-2025-0067 flags).[§](https://docs.rs#removed-in-006-vs-005)Removed in 0.0.6 (vs. 0.0.5)

The implementation-detail modules — `libyml::internal`,
`libyml::macros`, `libyml::externs`, `libyml::utils`,
`libyml::libc`, the contents of `libyml::memory` and
`libyml::string`, and the `yaml-test-suite` runner binaries
under `src/bin/` — are **gone** in this release. See
`MIGRATION.md` for the equivalence table per alternative.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [api](https://docs.rs/api/index.html)- Deprecated
- API-surface helpers. Re-exported from the crate root for source
compatibility with `libyml ≤ 0.0.5`’s`libyml::api`
- [decode](https://docs.rs/decode/index.html)- Deprecated
- Parser-decode helpers. Re-exported from the crate root for source
compatibility with `libyml ≤ 0.0.5`’s`libyml::decode`
- [document](https://docs.rs/document/index.html)- Deprecated
- Document-tree helpers. Re-exported from the crate root for source
compatibility with `libyml ≤ 0.0.5`’s`libyml::document`
- [dumper](https://docs.rs/dumper/index.html)- Deprecated
- Emitter dumper helpers. Re-exported from the crate root for source
compatibility with `libyml ≤ 0.0.5`’s`libyml::dumper`**Note:**the previous releases also exposed`yaml_emitter_dump_node`/`_scalar`/`_sequence`/`_mapping`as`pub`items; the upstream keeps those private. Callers should drive emission through the public`yaml_emitter_dump`entry point.
- [loader](https://docs.rs/loader/index.html)- Deprecated
- Event-loader helpers. Re-exported from the crate root for source
compatibility with `libyml ≤ 0.0.5`’s`libyml::loader`**Note:**the previous releases also exposed`yaml_parser_set_composer_error`as a`pub`item; the upstream surfaces composer errors through`yaml_parser_parse`/`yaml_parser_load`directly, so callers that constructed composer errors manually need to switch to inspecting`parser.problem`after the regular parse APIs return failure.
- [memory](https://docs.rs/memory/index.html)- Deprecated
- **Removed in 0.0.6.**Previous releases exposed a hand-translated C-libyaml allocator surface (- `yaml_malloc`/- `yaml_free`/- `yaml_realloc`/- `yaml_strdup`). Those helpers were implementation details of the hand-translated parser, which the 0.0.6 shim deletes; the upstream- `unsafe-libyaml`uses Rust’s- `alloc`directly. Allocate with Rust’s standard primitives instead. This empty module is retained so that- `use libyml::memory;`keeps resolving — every former item under it is gone.
- [string](https://docs.rs/string/index.html)- Deprecated
- **Removed in 0.0.6 — see**Previous releases exposed- `RUSTSEC-2025-0067`- `yaml_string_extend`/- `yaml_string_join`helpers under this path. The 0.0.6 shim deletes the entire hand-translated C copy that those helpers belonged to. Build strings with Rust’s- `Vec`/- `String`instead. This empty module is retained so- `use libyml::string;`keeps resolving — every former item under it is gone.
- [success](https://docs.rs/success/index.html)- Deprecated
- Success/failure helpers retained for source compatibility with
`libyml ≤ 0.0.5`.
- [yaml](https://docs.rs/yaml/index.html)- Deprecated
- Type aliases. Re-exported from the crate root for source
compatibility with `libyml ≤ 0.0.5`’s`libyml::yaml``Yaml*T`PascalCase types and`Yaml*`PascalCase enum variants land at this path too.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_alias_event_initialize.html)- alias_ - event_ - initialize - ⚠
- Create an ALIAS event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_document_delete.html)- document_ - delete - ⚠
- Delete a YAML document and all its nodes.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_document_end_event_initialize.html)- document_ - end_ - event_ - initialize - ⚠
- Create the DOCUMENT-END event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_document_get_node.html)- document_ - get_ - node - ⚠
- Get a node of a YAML document.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_document_get_root_node.html)- document_ - get_ - root_ - node - ⚠
- Get the root of a YAML document node.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_document_initialize.html)- document_ - initialize - ⚠
- Create a YAML document.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_document_start_event_initialize.html)- document_ - start_ - event_ - initialize - ⚠
- Create the DOCUMENT-START event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_close.html)- emitter_ - close - ⚠
- Finish a YAML stream.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_delete.html)- emitter_ - delete - ⚠
- Destroy an emitter.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_dump.html)- emitter_ - dump - ⚠
- Emit a YAML document.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_emit.html)- emitter_ - emit - ⚠
- Emit an event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_flush.html)- emitter_ - flush - ⚠
- Flush the accumulated characters to the output.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_initialize.html)- emitter_ - initialize - ⚠
- Initialize an emitter.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_open.html)- emitter_ - open - ⚠
- Start a YAML stream.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_break.html)- emitter_ - set_ - break - ⚠
- Set the preferred line break.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_canonical.html)- emitter_ - set_ - canonical - ⚠
- Set if the output should be in the “canonical” format as in the YAML specification.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_encoding.html)- emitter_ - set_ - encoding - ⚠
- Set the output encoding.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_indent.html)- emitter_ - set_ - indent - ⚠
- Set the indentation increment.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_output.html)- emitter_ - set_ - output - ⚠
- Set a generic output handler.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_output_string.html)- emitter_ - set_ - output_ - string - ⚠
- Set a string output.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_unicode.html)- emitter_ - set_ - unicode - ⚠
- Set if unescaped non-ASCII characters are allowed.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_emitter_set_width.html)- emitter_ - set_ - width - ⚠
- Set the preferred line width. -1 means unlimited.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_event_delete.html)- event_ - delete - ⚠
- Free any memory allocated for an event object.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_mapping_end_event_initialize.html)- mapping_ - end_ - event_ - initialize - ⚠
- Create a MAPPING-END event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_mapping_start_event_initialize.html)- mapping_ - start_ - event_ - initialize - ⚠
- Create a MAPPING-START event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_delete.html)- parser_ - delete - ⚠
- Destroy a parser.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_initialize.html)- parser_ - initialize - ⚠
- Initialize a parser.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_load.html)- parser_ - load - ⚠
- Parse the input stream and produce the next YAML document.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_parse.html)- parser_ - parse - ⚠
- Parse the input stream and produce the next parsing event.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_scan.html)- parser_ - scan - ⚠
- Scan the input stream and produce the next token.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_set_encoding.html)- parser_ - set_ - encoding - ⚠
- Set the source encoding.
- [yaml_](https://docs.rs/fn.yaml_parser_set_input.html)- parser_ - set_ - input - ⚠
- Set a generic input handler.

# libyml 0.0.6 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/libyml/latest/builds

All the builds on docs.rs are executed inside a sandbox with limited resources. The limits for this crate are the following:

| Available RAM | 6.44 GB |
| Maximum rustdoc execution time | 15m |
| Maximum size of a build log | 102.4 kB |
| Network access | blocked |
| Maximum number of build targets | 10 |

                    If a build fails because it hit one of those limits please
                    [open an issue](https://github.com/rust-lang/docs.rs/issues/new/choose)
                    to get them increased.

---

# libyml 0.0.5 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/libyml/0.0.5

# LibYML (a fork of unsafe-libyaml)

LibYML is a Rust library for working with YAML data, forked from [unsafe-libyaml](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml). It offers a safe and efficient interface for parsing, emitting, and manipulating YAML data.

## Features

- **Serialization and Deserialization**: Easy-to-use APIs for serializing Rust structs and enums to YAML and vice versa.
- **Custom Struct and Enum Support**: Seamless serialization and deserialization of custom data types.
- **Comprehensive Error Handling**: Detailed error messages and recovery mechanisms.
- **Streaming Support**: Efficient processing of large YAML documents.
- **Alias and Anchor Support**: Handling of complex YAML structures with references.
- **Tag Handling**: Support for custom tags and type-specific serialization.
- **Configurable Emitter**: Customizable YAML output generation.
- **Extensive Documentation**: Detailed docs and examples for easy onboarding.
- **Safety and Efficiency**: Minimized unsafe code with an interface designed to prevent common pitfalls.

## Installation

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "0.0.5"
```
## Usage

Here's a quick example on how to use LibYML to parse a YAML string:

```
use MaybeUninit;
use ;
```
## Documentation

For full API documentation, please visit [https://doc.libyml.com/libyml/](https://doc.libyml.com/libyml/) or [https://docs.rs/libyml](https://docs.rs/libyml).

## Rust Version Compatibility

Compiler support: requires rustc 1.56.0+

## Contributing

Contributions are welcome! If you'd like to contribute, please feel free to submit a Pull Request on [GitHub](https://github.com/sebastienrousseau/libyml).

## Credits and Acknowledgements

LibYML is a fork of the work done by [David Tolnay](https://github.com/dtolnay) and the maintainers of [unsafe-libyaml](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml). While it has evolved into a separate library, we express our sincere gratitude to them as well as the [libyaml](https://github.com/yaml/libyaml/tree/2c891fc7a770e8ba2fec34fc6b545c672beb37e6) maintainers for their contributions to the Rust and C programming communities.

## License

[MIT license](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT), same as libyaml.

---

# libyml 0.0.4 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/libyml/0.0.4

# LibYML (a fork of unsafe-libyaml)

This library is a fork of [unsafe-libyaml](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml), a version of [libyaml](https://github.com/yaml/libyaml/tree/2c891fc7a770e8ba2fec34fc6b545c672beb37e6)
translated from C to unsafe Rust with the assistance of [c2rust](https://github.com/immunant/c2rust).

This project, has been renamed to [LibYML](https://libyml.com) for simplicity and to avoid
confusion with the original [unsafe-libyaml](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml) crate which is now
archived and no longer maintained.

## Credits and Acknowledgements

This library is a fork of the excellent work done by [David Tolnay](https://github.com/dtolnay) and the
maintainers of the [unsafe-libyaml](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml) library.

LibYML has now evolved into a separate library with its own goals and direction in mind and does not intend to replace the original unsafe-libyaml crate.

If you are currently using unsafe-libyaml in your projects, we recommend carefully evaluating your requirements and considering the stability and maturity of the original library as well as looking at the features and improvements offered by other libraries in the Rust ecosystem.

I would like to express my sincere gratitude to [David Tolnay](https://github.com/dtolnay) and the
[unsafe-libyaml](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml) and [libyaml](https://github.com/yaml/libyaml/tree/2c891fc7a770e8ba2fec34fc6b545c672beb37e6) maintainers for their valuable
contributions to the Rust and C programming communities.

```
[]
 = "0.0.4"
```
Release notes are available under [GitHub releases](https://github.com/sebastienrousseau/libyml/releases).

### Rust Version Compatibility

This library is compatible with Rust 1.60 and above.

## Features

- **Serialization and Deserialization**: LibYML provides easy-to-use APIs for serializing Rust structs and enums into YAML format and deserializing YAML data into Rust types.
- **Custom Struct and Enum Support**: The library allows you to work with custom structs and enums, enabling seamless serialization and deserialization of your own data types.
- **Error Handling**: LibYML provides comprehensive error handling mechanisms, including detailed error messages and the ability to handle and recover from parsing and emission errors.
- **Streaming Support**: The library supports streaming of YAML data, allowing you to efficiently process large YAML documents incrementally.
- **Alias and Anchor Support**: LibYML handles YAML aliases and anchors, enabling you to work with complex YAML structures that involve references and duplicated data.
- **Tag Handling**: The library provides support for custom tags, allowing you to serialize and deserialize YAML data with specific type information.
- **Configurable Emitter**: LibYML allows you to customize the emitter settings, such as indentation, line width, and scalar style, to generate YAML output according to your preferences.
- **Extensive Documentation**: The library comes with detailed documentation and examples, making it easy to get started and understand how to use its various features effectively.
- **Safety and Efficiency**: LibYML is designed with safety and efficiency in mind. It minimizes the use of unsafe code and provides an interface that helps prevent common pitfalls and errors.

## Examples

To get started with LibYML, you can use the examples provided in the
`examples` directory of the project.

LibYML provides a set of comprehensive examples to demonstrate its usage and capabilities. The examples cover various aspects of the library, including initializing and deleting parsers, setting input strings, memory management, string manipulation, and more.

To run the examples, clone the repository and navigate to the examples directory. Each example is contained in a separate file, focusing on specific functionalities or use cases.

For instance, to run all the example demonstrating the usage of the LibYML APIs, you can execute the following command:

```
cargo run --example example
```
The command will execute all the examples code, demonstrating all the features and use cases of the LibYML library.

Here are a few notable examples you can also run individually:

### 1) The `apis` Example

The `api.rs` file provides a set of low-level API functions for working with
YAML data in the LibYML library. The `apis` example showcases the usage of
these low-level APIs covering functions such as:

- `yaml_parser_initialize`- Initialize a YAML parser,
- `yaml_parser_delete`- Delete a YAML parser,
- `yaml_parser_set_input_string`- Set the input string for the parser,
- `yaml_malloc`- Allocate memory,
- `yaml_realloc`- Reallocate memory,
- `yaml_free`- Free memory,
- `yaml_strdup`- Duplicate a string,
- `yaml_string_extend`- Extend a string,
- `yaml_string_join`- Join strings,

You can run the `apis` example using the following command:

```
cargo run --example apis
```
## License

[MIT license](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT), same as libyaml.

---

`examples` directory of the project.

LibYML provides a set of comprehensive examples to demonstrate its usage and capabilities. The examples cover various aspects of the library, including initializing and deleting parsers, setting input strings, memory management, string manipulation, and more.

To run the examples, clone the repository and navigate to the examples directory. Each example is contained in a separate file, focusing on specific functionalities or use cases.

For instance, to run all the example demonstrating the usage of the LibYML APIs, you can execute the following command:

```
cargo run --example example
```
The command will execute all the examples code, demonstrating all the features and use cases of the LibYML library.

Here are a few notable examples you can also run individually:

### 1) The `apis` Example

The `api.rs` file provides a set of low-level API functions for working with
YAML data in the LibYML library. The `apis` example showcases the usage of
these low-level APIs covering functions such as:

- `yaml_parser_initialize`- Initialize a YAML parser,
- `yaml_parser_delete`- Delete a YAML parser,
- `yaml_parser_set_input_string`- Set the input string for the parser,
- `yaml_malloc`- Allocate memory,
- `yaml_realloc`- Reallocate memory,
- `yaml_free`- Free memory,
- `yaml_strdup`- Duplicate a string,
- `yaml_string_extend`- Extend a string,
- `yaml_string_join`- Join strings,

You can run the `apis` example using the following command:

```

```

# libyml 0.0.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/libyml/0.0.2

# LibYML (a fork of unsafe-libyaml)

This library is a fork of [unsafe-libyaml](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml), a version of [libyaml](https://github.com/yaml/libyaml/tree/2c891fc7a770e8ba2fec34fc6b545c672beb37e6)
translated from C to unsafe Rust with the assistance of [c2rust](https://github.com/immunant/c2rust).

This project, has been renamed to [LibYML](https://libyml.com) for simplicity and to avoid
confusion with the original [unsafe-libyaml](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml) crate which is now
archived and no longer maintained.

## Credits and Acknowledgements

This library is a fork of the excellent work done by [David Tolnay](https://github.com/dtolnay) and the
maintainers of the [unsafe-libyaml](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml) library.

LibYML has now evolved into a separate library with its own goals and direction in mind and does not intend to replace the original unsafe-libyaml crate.

If you are currently using unsafe-libyaml in your projects, we recommend carefully evaluating your requirements and considering the stability and maturity of the original library as well as looking at the features and improvements offered by other libraries in the Rust ecosystem.

I would like to express my sincere gratitude to [David Tolnay](https://github.com/dtolnay) and the
[unsafe-libyaml](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml) and [libyaml](https://github.com/yaml/libyaml/tree/2c891fc7a770e8ba2fec34fc6b545c672beb37e6) maintainers for their valuable
contributions to the Rust and C programming communities.

```
[]
 = "0.0.2"
```
Release notes are available under [GitHub releases](https://github.com/sebastienrousseau/libyml/releases).

### Rust Version Compatibility

This library is compatible with Rust 1.60 and above.

## Features

- **Serialization and Deserialization**: LibYML provides easy-to-use APIs for serializing Rust structs and enums into YAML format and deserializing YAML data into Rust types.
- **Custom Struct and Enum Support**: The library allows you to work with custom structs and enums, enabling seamless serialization and deserialization of your own data types.
- **Error Handling**: LibYML provides comprehensive error handling mechanisms, including detailed error messages and the ability to handle and recover from parsing and emission errors.
- **Streaming Support**: The library supports streaming of YAML data, allowing you to efficiently process large YAML documents incrementally.
- **Alias and Anchor Support**: LibYML handles YAML aliases and anchors, enabling you to work with complex YAML structures that involve references and duplicated data.
- **Tag Handling**: The library provides support for custom tags, allowing you to serialize and deserialize YAML data with specific type information.
- **Configurable Emitter**: LibYML allows you to customize the emitter settings, such as indentation, line width, and scalar style, to generate YAML output according to your preferences.
- **Extensive Documentation**: The library comes with detailed documentation and examples, making it easy to get started and understand how to use its various features effectively.
- **Safety and Efficiency**: LibYML is designed with safety and efficiency in mind. It minimizes the use of unsafe code and provides an interface that helps prevent common pitfalls and errors.

## Examples

To get started with LibYML, you can use the examples provided in the
`examples` directory of the project.

LibYML provides a set of comprehensive examples to demonstrate its usage and capabilities. The examples cover various aspects of the library, including initializing and deleting parsers, setting input strings, memory management, string manipulation, and more.

To run the examples, clone the repository and navigate to the examples directory. Each example is contained in a separate file, focusing on specific functionalities or use cases.

For instance, to run all the example demonstrating the usage of the LibYML APIs, you can execute the following command:

```
cargo run --example example
```
The command will execute all the examples code, demonstrating all the features and use cases of the LibYML library.

Here are a few notable examples you can also run individually:

### 1) The `apis` Example

The `api.rs` file provides a set of low-level API functions for working with
YAML data in the LibYML library. The `apis` example showcases the usage of
these low-level APIs covering functions such as:

- `yaml_parser_initialize`- Initialize a YAML parser,
- `yaml_parser_delete`- Delete a YAML parser,
- `yaml_parser_set_input_string`- Set the input string for the parser,
- `yaml_malloc`- Allocate memory,
- `yaml_realloc`- Reallocate memory,
- `yaml_free`- Free memory,
- `yaml_strdup`- Duplicate a string,
- `yaml_string_extend`- Extend a string,
- `yaml_string_join`- Join strings,

You can run the `apis` example using the following command:

```
cargo run --example apis
```

# libyml 0.0.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/libyml/0.0.1

# LibYML

[ LibYML](https://libyml.com) is a Rust library for parsing and emitting YAML data in a safe and efficient manner. The library is designed to be easy to use and provides a comprehensive set of tools for working with YAML data.

• [Website](https://libyml.com) • [Documentation](https://docs.rs/libyml) • [Report Bug](https://github.com/sebastienrousseau/libyml/issues) • [Request Feature](https://github.com/sebastienrousseau/libyml/issues) • [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/sebastienrousseau/libyml/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

## Credits and Acknowledgements

[ LibYML](https://libyml.com) is a new library that draws inspiration from the excellent work done by

[David Tolnay](https://github.com/dtolnay)and the maintainers of the

[unsafe-libyaml](https://github.com/dtolnay/unsafe-libyaml)library. I would like to express my sincere gratitude to David and the

`unsafe-libyaml` team for their valuable contributions to the Rust community.While LibYML started as a fork of `unsafe-libyaml`, it has evolved into a separate library with its own goals and direction. The primary intent behind creating LibYML was to provide an actively maintained and enhanced library for working with YAML data in Rust, while also serving as a learning opportunity.

It's important to note that LibYML is not intended to replace `unsafe-libyaml`. If you are currently using `unsafe-libyaml` in your projects, we recommend carefully evaluating your requirements and considering the stability and maturity of the original library before migrating to LibYML.

We acknowledge and appreciate the significant work done by David Tolnay and the `unsafe-libyaml` maintainers. Their efforts have been instrumental in laying the foundation for LibYML and inspiring its development.

## Overview

`LibYML` is a robust Rust library that provides a comprehensive set of tools for working with YAML data. The library offers a wide range of features, including serialization, deserialization, custom struct and enum support, error handling, and more.

## Features

- **Serialization and Deserialization**: LibYML provides easy-to-use APIs for serializing Rust structs and enums into YAML format and deserializing YAML data into Rust types.
- **Custom Struct and Enum Support**: The library allows you to work with custom structs and enums, enabling seamless serialization and deserialization of your own data types.
- **Error Handling**: LibYML provides comprehensive error handling mechanisms, including detailed error messages and the ability to handle and recover from parsing and emission errors.
- **Streaming Support**: The library supports streaming of YAML data, allowing you to efficiently process large YAML documents incrementally.
- **Alias and Anchor Support**: LibYML handles YAML aliases and anchors, enabling you to work with complex YAML structures that involve references and duplicated data.
- **Tag Handling**: The library provides support for custom tags, allowing you to serialize and deserialize YAML data with specific type information.
- **Configurable Emitter**: LibYML allows you to customize the emitter settings, such as indentation, line width, and scalar style, to generate YAML output according to your preferences.
- **Extensive Documentation**: The library comes with detailed documentation and examples, making it easy to get started and understand how to use its various features effectively.
- **Safety and Efficiency**: LibYML is designed with safety and efficiency in mind. It minimizes the use of unsafe code and provides an interface that helps prevent common pitfalls and errors.

### Rust Version Compatibility

This library is compatible with Rust 1.60 and above.

## Usage

LibYML offers a straightforward and intuitive API for working with YAML data in Rust. To get started, add the following dependency to your `Cargo.toml` file:

```
[]
 = "0.0.1"
```
## Examples

To get started with LibYML, you can use the examples provided in the `examples` directory of the project.

LibYML provides a set of comprehensive examples to demonstrate its usage and capabilities. The examples cover various aspects of the library, including initializing and deleting parsers, setting input strings, memory management, string manipulation, and more.

To run the examples, clone the repository and navigate to the examples directory. Each example is contained in a separate file, focusing on specific functionalities or use cases.

For instance, to run all the example demonstrating the usage of the LibYML APIs, you can execute the following command:

```
cargo run --example example
```
The command will execute all the examples code, demonstrating all the features and use cases of the LibYML library.

Here are a few notable examples you can also run individually:

### 1) The `apis` Example

The `api.rs` file provides a set of low-level API functions for working with YAML data in the LibYML library. The `apis` example showcases the usage of these low-level APIs covering functions such as:

- `yaml_parser_initialize`- Initialize a YAML parser,
- `yaml_parser_delete`- Delete a YAML parser,
- `yaml_parser_set_input_string`- Set the input string for the parser,
- `yaml_malloc`- Allocate memory,
- `yaml_realloc`- Reallocate memory,
- `yaml_free`- Free memory,
- `yaml_strdup`- Duplicate a string,
- `yaml_string_extend`- Extend a string,
- `yaml_string_join`- Join strings,

You can run the `apis` example using the following command:

```

```

# yaml_rust2 - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/yaml-rust2

## Expand description

YAML 1.2 implementation in pure Rust.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

This crate is [on github](https://github.com/Ethiraric/yaml-rust2) and can be used by adding
`yaml-rust2` to the dependencies in your project’s `Cargo.toml`.

`cargo add yaml-rust2`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Parse a string into `Vec<Yaml>` and then serialize it as a YAML string.

```
use yaml_rust2::{YamlLoader, YamlEmitter};
let docs = YamlLoader::load_from_str("[1, 2, 3]").unwrap();
let doc = &docs[0]; // select the first YAML document
assert_eq!(doc[0].as_i64().unwrap(), 1); // access elements by index
let mut out_str = String::new();
let mut emitter = YamlEmitter::new(&mut out_str);
emitter.dump(doc).unwrap(); // dump the YAML object to a String
```
[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

**Note:** With all features disabled, this crate’s MSRV is `1.65.0`.

[§](https://docs.rs#encoding-enabled-by-default)`encoding` (*enabled by default*)

Enables encoding-aware decoding of Yaml documents.

The MSRV for this feature is `1.65.0`.

[§](https://docs.rs#debug_prints)`debug_prints`

Enables the `debug` module and usage of debug prints in the scanner and the parser. Do not
enable if you are consuming the crate rather than working on it as this can significantly
decrease performance.

The MSRV for this feature is `1.70.0`.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use crate::emitter::`- [EmitError](https://docs.rs/emitter/enum.EmitError.html);
- `pub use crate::emitter::`- [YamlEmitter](https://docs.rs/emitter/struct.YamlEmitter.html);
- `pub use crate::parser::`- [Event](https://docs.rs/parser/enum.Event.html);
- `pub use crate::scanner::`- [ScanError](https://docs.rs/scanner/struct.ScanError.html);
- `pub use crate::yaml::`- [Yaml](https://docs.rs/yaml/enum.Yaml.html);
- `pub use crate::yaml::`- [YamlLoader](https://docs.rs/yaml/struct.YamlLoader.html);
